headline: The US government's energy forecaster expects wholesale electricity prices in the largest US power market, PJM, to rise 41 percent in 2026.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered to 5: the headline blames the AI boom, but the article says weather explains much of the rise and the source is an investor commentary on a forecast.
importance_line: People in the PJM region may pay more for power over time, but wholesale prices are not household bills, weather explains much of the rise and only part comes from data centres, and it is a forecast, not a result.
summary: 24/7 Wall St. reports that the US Energy Information Administration's October outlook forecasts 2026 wholesale power prices in PJM up 41 percent on 2025, the biggest rise of any region it tracks, against an 11 percent rise to $52 per megawatt-hour for the US average. The agency puts much of the rise down to an unusually hot summer and winter storms, so data centres are only part of the cause, and household bills follow their own path because they also cover transmission, local delivery and capacity costs.
notes: EIA's own outlook was not opened; figures are as reported by 24/7 Wall St. PJM is the grid operator for 13 US states.
